title: Chart-compatible blowup immersion from a graded Rees presentation
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], and $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\to X$ the ordinary glued blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra with $\mathcal C_0=\mathcal O_X$ [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Suppose that, for every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, with $I_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal I)$, a graded $R$-algebra isomorphism
$$\theta_V:\Gamma(V,\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal R_R(I_V)$$
is given [def-nagata-rees-algebra], is the identity in degree zero, and commutes with affine restrictions via coefficientwise restriction of Rees algebras; on $D(s)\subseteq V$ this restriction sends $xt^n$ to $(x/1)t^n$. Suppose also that $\varphi:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I)\to\mathcal C$ is a degree-preserving morphism surjective in every degree on affine opens, where the source has the canonical symmetric grading [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra].

There is a unique isomorphism $e:B\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal C)$ over $X$ [def-nagata-relative-proj] whose restriction over each affine $V$ is the contravariant Proj isomorphism induced by $\theta_V$, with the canonical local identification $b^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_R(I_V))$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. In particular, these local isomorphisms agree on arbitrary overlaps, interpreted through affine refinements. Applying relative Proj to $\varphi$ and composing with $e$ defines a closed immersion over $X$
$$j:B\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}_X(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I))=\mathbf P_X(\mathcal I).$$
Here $\mathbf P_X(\mathcal I)$ is the projective bundle of [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. The restriction of $j$ over each affine $V$ is the Proj morphism of $\operatorname{Sym}_R(I_V)\xrightarrow{\varphi_V}\Gamma(V,\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\theta_V}\mathcal R_R(I_V)$, and the projective-bundle projection composed with $j$ is $b$. No integrality, Noetherian or nonzero-ideal hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n$. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-rees-symmetric-presentation] to obtain the graded coefficient isomorphisms $\alpha_V:\Gamma(V,\mathcal R)\simeq\mathcal R_R(I_V)$, identity in degree zero and compatible with all affine restrictions. Apply [lem-sfb-blowup-rees-symmetric-presentation] to obtain $e_0:B\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal R)$ over $X$. Its affine restriction is the coefficient identification, so the comorphism of $(e_0)_V$ on homogeneous localizations is induced by $\alpha_V$. These results assume only that $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent; in particular the given finite-type ideal satisfies their hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective), displayed Rees algebra and identification of the blowup with its relative Proj

proof.text:
For every affine $V$, set $\gamma_V=\alpha_V^{-1}\theta_V:\Gamma(V,\mathcal C)\simeq\Gamma(V,\mathcal R)$. For an affine inclusion $W\subseteq V$, both $\alpha$ and $\theta$ intertwine restriction with the same coefficientwise Rees restriction; cancelling $\alpha_W$ gives $\gamma_W\operatorname{res}_{\mathcal C}=\operatorname{res}_{\mathcal R}\gamma_V$. The inverse maps satisfy the inverse equality. Thus these maps give a base-linear graded isomorphism $\gamma:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal R$ in the affine-basis presentation. Use [def-sfb-relative-proj-iso-of-graded-iso] to form $F:\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal R)\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal C)$ and set $e=F\circ e_0$. For homogeneous $f\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal C)_d$, $d>0$, its chart comorphism is
$$a/f^m\longmapsto\gamma_V(a)/\gamma_V(f)^m\longmapsto\alpha_V\gamma_V(a)/(\alpha_V\gamma_V(f))^m=\theta_V(a)/\theta_V(f)^m.$$
Hence $e_V$ is precisely the contravariant Proj isomorphism of $\theta_V$, not just an unspecified isomorphism of the local schemes. It lies over $X$, since its maps on degree-zero scalars are the identity and the structural maps of [def-nagata-relative-proj] are induced by these scalars.

source.place: Tags 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), 01MZ (lemma-morphism-proj-transitive), 01NQ (lemma-glue-relative-proj); specialization to the composite graded isomorphism

proof.text: For affine $V,W\subseteq X$, cover $V\cap W$ by affine opens $T\subseteq V\cap W$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The restriction compatibility in [def-sfb-relative-proj-iso-of-graded-iso], the compatibility of $e_0$ from Step 1, and the identity $\alpha_T\gamma_T=\theta_T$ show that both local restrictions of $e$ on $b^{-1}(T)$ are the map of $\theta_T$. Therefore they agree on $b^{-1}(V\cap W)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. If $e'$ has the required affine restrictions, its underlying morphism equals $e$ on every $b^{-1}(V)$; these opens cover $B$, so the same gluing uniqueness gives $e'=e$. The inverse of an isomorphism is determined by its forward map, which proves uniqueness as an isomorphism. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 01NQ (lemma-glue-relative-proj), affine restrictions; uniqueness from gluing morphisms on the inverse-image open cover

proof.text:
On each affine $V$, every element of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal C)$ is a finite sum of homogeneous elements. Lift each summand in its degree under $\varphi_V$ and sum the lifts. Thus the assumed degreewise surjectivity implies surjectivity of the whole graded algebra map on every affine open. Apply clause (3) of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] to obtain the induced closed immersion
$$q:\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal C)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}_X(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I)).$$
Define $j=q\circ e$.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective), application of the surjective relative-Proj theorem; Constructions Tag 07ZK (lemma-surjective-generated-degree-1-map-relative-proj)

proof.text:
Let $A=\operatorname{Sym}_R(I_V)$. The canonical symmetric grading [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] has $A_n=(\operatorname{im}\iota)^n$, so $A$ is generated by $A_1$ over $R$. Apply the chart assertion of [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison] to the surjective map $\varphi_V:A\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal C)$. For $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, its chart comorphism is $a/f^m\mapsto\varphi_V(a)/\varphi_V(f)^m$. Composing with the Step 2 chart map for $e$ gives
$$a/f^m\longmapsto (\theta_V\varphi_V)(a)/(\theta_V\varphi_V)(f)^m.$$
The inverse-image chart is $D_+((\theta_V\varphi_V)(f))$, so this identifies $j_V$ with the Proj morphism of the asserted composite, including its domain charts. These formulas fix every base scalar $r\in R$ because $\varphi_V$ and $\theta_V$ are $R$-linear. By the structural-map description in [def-nagata-relative-proj], the projection composed with $j$ equals $b$ over every affine $V$; gluing uniqueness [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives the equality globally. Finally [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] identifies the target with $\mathbf P_X(\mathcal I)$; its finite-type quasi-coherent module hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $\mathcal I$.

source.place: Tags 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj) and 07ZK (lemma-surjective-generated-degree-1-map-relative-proj), affine chart formulas; divisors.tex Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective), target projective bundle

proof.text: The composite $j=q\circ e$ is a closed immersion directly from [def-weil-closed-immersion]: its underlying map is the homeomorphism $e$ followed by the homeomorphism of $q$ onto its closed image. For its structure sheaf map, the map for $q$ is surjective and the subsequent map induced by the scheme isomorphism $e$ is an isomorphism. Their composite is surjective. Thus $j$ has both defining properties of a closed immersion. This uses no condition on the ideal beyond those already stated.
